Condo renovation in Vancouver—where 62% of Metro Vancouver's 270,000+ apartment and condo residents live in strata-titled properties, making Vancouver one of the most strata-dense cities in Canada—ranges in cost from $10,000 for a cosmetic refresh to over $150,000 for a complete unit gut renovation involving kitchen, bathroom, flooring, electrical, and structural modifications. For a typical Vancouver condo renovation in 2026, a mid-range project covering kitchen cabinet replacement, bathroom renovation, flooring throughout, and fresh paint costs $25,000 to $55,000, while a complete gut renovation including structural modifications, new electrical panels, and full mechanical updates can reach $80,000 to $150,000. Reno Stars has been completing condo renovation projects across Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and the North Shore since 2015, and Vancouver condo owners should understand that strata approval is required before any work begins on common property or limited common property elements, that Vancouver building permits are required for any work affecting structural elements or fire-rated assemblies, and that the BC Strata Property Act gives strata councils specific authority over renovations that affect the common elements of the building.

Strata Approval Process for Vancouver Condo Renovation

Every condo renovation in Vancouver must navigate the strata approval process, which is governed by the BC Strata Property Act and the specific bylaws of each individual strata corporation:

  • The BC Strata Property Act distinguishes between limited common property (elements assigned for the exclusive use of one unit, such as a balcony or parking stall) and common property (elements shared by all owners, such as hallways, elevators, and building systems). Work on limited common property requires strata council approval; work on common property requires a 3/4 vote of the strata corporation.
  • Vancouver strata corporations typically have detailed renovation bylaws specifying what work can proceed with only strata council approval (routine cosmetic work) versus what requires a general meeting vote (work affecting structural elements, fire-rated assemblies, plumbing risers, or building exterior).
  • The strata approval process in Vancouver typically takes 2–6 weeks from application to decision, depending on the complexity of the renovation and the strata council's meeting schedule. Some Vancouver strata buildings have pre-approved renovation packages for common work types that can proceed faster.
  • Common renovation items requiring strata council approval in Vancouver include: any work requiring a Vancouver building permit, changes to balcony or patio enclosures, installation of flooring materials that may affect neighbouring units (hardwood, tile), and any work affecting the building exterior or common property elements.
  • Items requiring a 3/4 vote in Vancouver include: modifications to fire-rated wall assemblies, changes to shared plumbing or electrical systems, removal or modification of structural walls, and any work affecting the building's exterior envelope or common mechanical spaces.
  • Vancouver's Strata Property Act allows strata corporations to impose monetary penalties for unauthorized renovations—owners who proceed without required approvals can face fines and orders to restore the unit to its original condition at the owner's expense.
  • For Vancouver condo buyers, a thorough review of the strata's renovation bylaws and any existing bylaw contraventions should be completed before purchasing, as some Vancouver condos have significant restrictions on what renovations are permitted.
  • Reno Stars assists Vancouver condo renovation clients with the complete strata approval process, including preparing renovation proposals, attending strata council meetings, and coordinating with the strata property management company.

Vancouver Condo Renovation Costs (2026)

Condo renovation costs in Vancouver vary widely based on the scope of work, the size of the unit, and the quality of finishes chosen:

  • Kitchen renovation (mid-range Vancouver condo, 150–250 sq ft kitchen): $15,000–$40,000 including cabinetry, countertops, appliance installation, backsplash, lighting, and flooring
  • Full bathroom renovation (Vancouver condo, 40–80 sq ft bathroom): $8,000–$25,000 including waterproofing, tiling, fixtures, vanity, toilet, and exhaust fan
  • Second bathroom addition (where plumbing rough-in exists): $12,000–$30,000
  • Complete flooring replacement (Vancouver condo, 600–1,000 sq ft): $4,000–$12,000 for vinyl plank, $6,000–$15,000 for hardwood, $5,000–$14,000 for tile
  • Electrical panel upgrade (100 amp to 200 amp): $1,500–$4,000 in Vancouver, including licensed electrician and permit
  • Drywall repair and painting (full condo): $2,000–$6,000 for prep, paint, and labour
  • Closet system installation: $1,500–$5,000 per closet
  • Balcony enclosure or renovation (Vancouver climate-rated): $5,000–$15,000
  • Structural modification (removing a non-load-bearing wall): $3,000–$8,000 including engineering and Vancouver building permit
  • Complete gut renovation (Vancouver condo, 700–1,200 sq ft): $60,000–$150,000

Vancouver Building Permit Requirements for Condo Renovation

Building permit requirements for condo renovation in Vancouver differ from single-family homes due to the shared nature of the building:

  • Cosmetic work (painting, wallpaper,更换 flooring without building structure changes) does NOT require a Vancouver building permit in a condo.
  • Kitchen and bathroom renovation involving plumbing fixture changes (toilet, sink, shower/tub relocation) requires a Vancouver building permit and must comply with BC Plumbing Code.
  • Any work affecting fire-rated assemblies in a Vancouver condo—including the wall between the unit and the corridor, the ceiling assembly, and the floor assembly—must maintain or improve the fire rating and requires a Vancouver building permit.
  • Electrical work in a Vancouver condo (new circuits, panel upgrades, pot light installation) requires a Technical Safety BC electrical permit and must be completed by a licensed electrician.
  • Structural modifications in a Vancouver condo—including removal of any wall, even a non-load-bearing partition—always requires a Vancouver building permit and a P.Eng structural assessment, plus strata approval.
  • The BC Building Code Part 9 applies to most Vancouver condo renovations, setting minimum standards for structural safety, fire separation, ventilation, and energy efficiency.
  • Vancouver building permit processing time for condo renovations is typically 2–4 weeks for standard scope, longer for complex structural modifications.
  • A final inspection by the City of Vancouver is required for any permit work, and the permit holder is responsible for arranging the inspection through the City's permit portal.

Frequently Asked Questions About Condo Renovation in Vancouver

Can I renovate my Vancouver condo without strata approval?

No—proceeding with a Vancouver condo renovation without the required strata approval can result in significant financial penalties, a legal order to restore the unit to its original condition, and potential difficulty selling the unit in the future. Under the BC Strata Property Act, a Vancouver strata corporation can impose fines of up to $500 per violation per day for unauthorized renovations, and the strata can apply to the BC Supreme Court for an order requiring the owner to undo the work at their own expense. The scope of work requiring strata approval depends on your specific strata corporation's bylaws, which vary significantly between Vancouver buildings. Cosmetic work like painting and installing new flooring may only require strata council approval, while work affecting common property, limited common property, fire-rated assemblies, or structural elements requires a formal general meeting vote with 3/4 approval from owners. Reno Stars always confirms the specific approval requirements with the strata property management company before beginning any Vancouver condo renovation project.

What Vancouver building permits do I need for a condo renovation?

The Vancouver building permits required for a condo renovation depend on the scope of work. Cosmetic work—painting, wallpapering, and replacing flooring without structural changes—does not require a Vancouver building permit. However, any work involving plumbing fixture changes, electrical modifications, fire-rated assembly alterations, or structural changes requires a Vancouver building permit and must comply with the BC Building Code and BC Plumbing Code. Electrical work additionally requires a Technical Safety BC electrical permit and must be performed by a licensed electrician registered in Vancouver. Structural modifications—including removing any wall, even a non-load-bearing partition—require a registered professional engineer's assessment, a Vancouver building permit application, and mandatory City of Vancouver inspections. The permit application must include drawings showing the existing and proposed conditions, and for work in a Vancouver condo building, the permit application may also need to include confirmation that strata approval has been obtained. Processing time at the City of Vancouver is typically 2–4 weeks for standard renovation permits, longer for complex structural work.

How much does a complete condo renovation cost in Vancouver in 2026?

A complete gut renovation of a Vancouver condo unit in 2026 costs $60,000 to $150,000 for a 700–1,200 square foot unit, depending on finish quality and scope complexity. This includes complete removal of all existing finishes, new electrical wiring and panel upgrade, new plumbing rough-in if fixtures are being relocated, new drywall, new kitchen with cabinetry and appliances, one to two renovated bathrooms, new flooring throughout, fresh paint, and trim work. A mid-range renovation covering kitchen cabinet and countertop replacement, full bathroom renovation, new flooring, and painting typically costs $25,000 to $55,000 in Vancouver. A cosmetic refresh—new paint, flooring replacement, and bathroom fixture updates—typically costs $10,000 to $25,000. These costs include Vancouver contractor labour and materials but do not include furniture, window treatments, or appliances unless specifically stated. Strata approval costs, Vancouver building permit fees, and engineering assessments are additional and typically add $2,000 to $6,000 to the total project cost in Vancouver.
